name: AeroSpace
summary: i3-like tiling window manager for macOS. Tree of tiles/accordion containers, its own virtual workspaces instead of native Spaces, plain TOML config and a CLI. Needs no SIP changes. Public beta.

install.notes: brew install --cask nikitabobko/tap/aerospace. The cask removes the quarantine flag (the app is not notarized). Needs macOS 13+.

macos.notes: Grant AeroSpace.app the Accessibility permission (System Settings, Privacy and Security) on first launch; it is asked again after an update that changes the code-sign certificate. There is no config file until you create one: copy /Applications/AeroSpace.app/Contents/Resources/default-config.toml to ~/.aerospace.toml. Uses its own virtual workspaces, so macOS Spaces and Mission Control swipes do not map to AeroSpace workspaces; keep one macOS Space. With 'Displays have separate Spaces' on, multi-monitor behavior is less stable (docs recommend turning it off, logout needed). Native fullscreen windows create their own Space and escape tiling. No built-in borders, shadows, opacity or animations (by design). No validate entry: 'aerospace reload-config --dry-run --no-gui' checks the active config at its normal path, not a draft file, so run it after staging.

borders.notes: AeroSpace deliberately has no window borders. Companion tool: JankyBorders (brew tap FelixKratz/formulae; brew install borders), macOS 14+. Start it from AeroSpace by adding to ~/.aerospace.toml: after-startup-command = ['exec-and-forget borders active_color=0xffRRGGBB inactive_color=0xffRRGGBB width=5.0'], with active_color = the look's {palette.accent} and inactive_color = {palette.ansi.brightBlack}, each written as 0xff followed by the hex without the #. Colors are 0xAARRGGBB.
